short: An abortive coup d'état led by the Earl of Essex in the final years of Elizabeth I's reign.
full:
Robert Devereux, 2nd Earl of Essex, had long been a favourite of Elizabeth I, but his relationship with the Queen deteriorated following his disastrous military campaign in Ireland and his subsequent unauthorised return to court. Stripped of his monopolies and facing financial ruin, Essex formulated a desperate plan to seize control of the government, oust his political rivals led by Sir Robert Cecil, and force the aging Queen to declare James VI of Scotland her heir.

On 8 February 1601, Essex marched into London with a small force of armed supporters, hoping the city's populace would rise in his favour. The anticipated support failed to materialise, and the government swiftly declared him a traitor. Essex was forced to surrender after a brief skirmish at his home. He was tried for treason and beheaded at the Tower of London later that month, marking the last major political upheaval of the Elizabethan era.
